overview.description: Dai Fugo (大富豪, 'Grand Millionaire') is a Japanese climbing/shedding game for 3–8 players. Similar to President: play single cards or sets of same rank; next player must play same number of higher rank or pass. First to empty hand is Dai Fugō (Grand Millionaire); last is Dai Hinmin (Very Poor). Card exchange between rounds based on finish position.
overview.originName: 大富豪 (Dai Fugō) — Japanese for Grand Millionaire

history.origins: Dai Fugo is a Japanese card game likely introduced from China in the 1970s. It became popular throughout Japan in the 1980s and 1990s. The game is the likely ancestor of President (also known as Asshole), which became popular in the West a few years later.
timeline: 1970s: Game likely introduced from China to Japan
Present: Popular in Japan and internationally
history.evolution: Numerous additional rules and variations were introduced during its peak popularity in Japan. The Revolution (kakumei) rule—where four of a kind reverses card rankings—is a major modern addition.
history.cultural: The player titles (Dai Fugō, Fugō, Heimin, Hinmin, Dai Hinmin) reflect economic hierarchy. Commonly played without score or payment—the aim is simply to be as rich as possible as often as possible.

setup.players: 3–8 (ideally 4–6). All cards dealt; remainder to first dealer if uneven.
setup.deck: 52 cards plus 1–2 jokers. Rank: Joker highest, then 2, A, K, Q, J, 10 down to 3. Suits irrelevant.
setup.dealing: All cards dealt as evenly as possible. Player to dealer's left leads first (or loser of previous hand).

rules.objective: Be the first to play all your cards. Finish order determines titles for next round (Dai Fugō, Fugō, Heimin, Hinmin, Dai Hinmin).
rules.gameplay: Lead any single card or valid combination (pair, three of a kind, four of a kind, or sequence of 3+ consecutive cards of same suit). Next player must play same number of cards of higher rank or pass. Once passed, cannot play until the round ends. When all but one pass, that player leads next. First out wins the round.
keyRules: Rank: Joker > 2 > A > K > Q > J > 10 > … > 3
Play same number of cards, higher rank, or pass
Sequences must be same suit, 3+ cards
Dai Hinmin → Dai Fugō: 2 cards; Hinmin → Fugō: 1 card

strategy.basic: Get rid of low cards when you can; save high cards for when you must beat. The 3 is the weakest card—try to play it early when no one needs to beat it.
strategy.intermediate: Track what has been played; pass when you can't win the round to save cards. Watch for opportunities to play sequences which are harder to beat than single cards.
strategy.advanced: Manage your hand for the exchange. If you're likely to be Dai Hinmin, try to keep some medium cards that won't be taken but can still win tricks. The Revolution rule (if used) dramatically changes strategy—four of a kind becomes a powerful game-changer.
tips: Save your 2s and Jokers for critical moments—they're your trump cards
If you have multiple 3s, consider playing them as a set rather than singles
Leading a high sequence can clear the table and give you control
After a revolution, the 2 becomes the weakest card—adjust your strategy immediately

list.name: Revolution (Kakumei)
list.description: Four of a kind causes revolution, reversing card rankings (3 becomes highest, 2 lowest). Second revolution restores original order.

difficulty.easy: Plays lowest legal card or combination. Doesn't plan for exchanges.
difficulty.medium: Balances playing low cards with saving winners. Understands exchange implications. Basic revolution timing.
difficulty.hard: Optimal hand management for exchanges. Perfect tracking of played cards. Knows when to trigger or avoid revolution.

considerations: Card exchange impact on next round

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy identification.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where each rank has distinct value and meaning depending on the specific game rules and player strategies.

hero.title: DAI FUGO
hero.subtitle: Grand Millionaire
hero.tagline: Climb the social ladder—be the first to shed your cards and claim your title.

synthesis.shortDescription: A Japanese climbing game where players race to empty their hands. Finish order determines your title for the next round, with the Dai Fugō getting advantages in card exchange.

prompts.human: Play Dai Fugo! Get rid of all your cards first to become the Grand Millionaire. Play singles, pairs, or sequences—but they must be higher than the last play. Watch out for the card exchange before each new round!
prompts.ai: Game: Dai Fugo. Type: Shedding/Climbing. 3-8 players. Rank: Joker>2>A>K>Q>J>10>...>3. Play higher combination or pass. First out=Dai Fugō, last=Dai Hinmin. Exchange: Dai Hinmin gives 2 best to Dai Fugō; Hinmin gives 1 to Fugō.

scoring.description: No points in basic game. Finish order sets titles; titles determine card exchange and who leads next round. Optional scoring: Dai Fugō +2, Fugō +1.
scoring.winCondition: Be the first to empty your hand.
